Title: Comparative transcriptome analysis of latex from rubber tree clone CATAS8-79 and PR107 reveals new cues for the regulation of latex regeneration and duration of latex flow.

Journal/Date: BMC plant biology (2015)

MeSH Keywords: Gene Expression, Genes, Plant, Latex, Rubber, Transcriptome, Trees


--- ABSTRACT ---
[BACKGROUND]: Rubber tree (Hevea brasiliensis Muell. Arg.) is the primarily commercial source of natural rubber in the world. Latex regeneration and duration of latex flow after tapping are the two factors that determine rubber yield of rubber tree, and exhibit a huge variation between rubber tree clones CATAS8-79 and PR107.
[RESULTS]: To dissect the molecular mechanism for the regulation of latex regeneration and duration of latex flow, we sequenced and comparatively analyzed latex of rubber tree clone CATAS8-79 and PR107 at transriptome level. More than 26 million clean reads were generated in each pool and 51,829 all-unigenes were totally assembled. A total of 6,726 unigenes with differential expression patterns were detected between CATAS8-79 and PR107. Functional analysis showed that genes related to mass of categories were differentially enriched between the two clones. Expression pattern of genes which were involved in latex regeneration and duration of latex flow upon successive tapping was analyzed by quantitative PCR. Several genes related to rubber biosynthesis, cellulose and lignin biosynthesis and rubber particle aggregation were differentially expressed between CATAS8-79 and PR107.
[CONCLUSIONS]: This is the first report about probing latex regeneration and duration of latex flow by comparative transcriptome analysis. Among all the suggested factors, it is more important that the level of endogenous jasmonates, carbohydrate metabolism, hydroxymethylglutaryl-CoA reductase (HMGR) and Hevea rubber transferase (HRT) in mevalonate (MVA) parthway for latex regeneration while the level of endogenous ethylene (ETH), lignin content of laticifer cell wall, antioxidants and glucanases for the duration of latex flow. These data will provide new cues for understanding the molecular mechanism for the regulation of latex regeneration and duration of latex flow in rubber tree.

Title: Transcript and Protein Profiling Provides Insights Into the Molecular Mechanisms of Harvesting-Induced Latex Production in Rubber Tree.

Journal/Date: Frontiers in genetics (2022)

MeSH Keywords: None listed


--- ABSTRACT ---
Natural rubber, an important industrial raw material with wide applications, is harvested in the form of latex (cytoplasm of rubber-producing laticifers) from Hevea brasiliensis (para rubber tree) by the way of tapping. Conspicuous stimulation on latex production is observed for the first few tappings conducted on virgin (untapped before) or resting (tapped before but no tapping for a period) rubber trees. To understand the underlying mechanisms, an integrative analysis of the latex transcriptome and proteome was conducted on virgin or resting Hevea trees for the first five tappings. A total of 505 non-redundant differentially expressed (DE) transcript-derived fragments (TDFs) were identified by silver-staining cDNA-AFLP, with 217 exhibiting patterns of upregulated, 180 downregulated and 108 irregularly-regulated. Meanwhile, 117 two dimensional gel electrophoresis DE-protein spots were isolated and subjected to mass spectrometry analysis, with 89 and 57 being successfully identified by MALDI-TOF and MALDI-TOF/TOF, respectively. About 72.5% DE-TDFs and 76.1% DE-proteins were functionally annotated and categorized. Noteworthily, most of the DE-TDFs implicated in sugar transport and metabolism as well as rubber biosynthesis were upregulated by the tapping treatment. The importance of sugar metabolism in harvesting-induced latex production was reinforced by the identification of abundant relevant DE-protein spots. About 83.8% of the randomly selected DE-TDFs were validated for expression patterns by semi-quantitative RT-PCR, and an 89.7% consistency for the 29 latex regeneration-related DE-TDFs examined by quantitative RT-PCR analysis. In brief, our results reveal extensive physiological and molecular changes in Hevea laticifers incurred by the tapping treatment, and the vast number of DE genes and proteins identified here contribute to unraveling the gene regulatory network of tapping-stimulated latex production.

Results

Screening of Differentially Expressed Transcripts and Proteins

To extensively identify the differentially expressed transcripts responding to the tapping treatment, all the 128 cDNA-AFLP selective primer pairs of Apo I / Mse I restriction system were screened in the latex RNA for the first five tappings in virgin Hevea trees. Therefore, nearly 9,000 TDFs were profiled for each latex RNA sample. In total, 651 DE-TDFs were successfully cloned and sequenced.

key_findings.finding: Direct comparative evidence exists that clone-level differences in sustained latex flow/regeneration have transcriptomic correlates. PMID 25928745 compared latex from CATAS8-79 and PR107, clones differing in latex regeneration and flow duration; 6,726 DE unigenes were found. The authors implicated endogenous jasmonates, carbohydrate metabolism, HMGR and HRT/MVA-pathway activity mainly in regeneration, and endogenous ethylene, laticifer-wall lignin, antioxidants, glucanases, rubber biosynthesis, cellulose/lignin biosynthesis, and rubber-particle aggregation in flow duration. This is the strongest direct transcriptomic study of prolonged flow, but it is a clone comparison with mechanistic candidates rather than causal validation.

source_tools.relevance: Abstract and study conclusions directly describe the clone comparison, DEG count, and candidate mechanisms for regeneration versus duration of flow.

key_findings.finding: A second yield-comparison study supports related mechanisms but does not isolate prolonged flow. PMID 24066172 compared a super-high-yield PR107 tree (SY107; 4.12 kg latex/tapping) with average controls using cDNA-AFLP: 746 DE fragments, 453 RT-PCR-confirmed, representing 352 genes. The high-yield phenotype was associated with improved sucrose loading, sugar utilization favoring rubber production, general metabolism, and stress alleviation, with little correlation to canonical rubber-biosynthesis genes; flow duration itself was not the primary comparison.

source_tools.relevance: Primary study abstract and results preview provide the experimental comparison, yield contrast, DEG numbers, and interpretation.

key_findings.finding: Self-rooting juvenile versus donor-clone latex RNA-seq also supports improved latex metabolism/flow, not specifically sustained flow. PMID 27555864 identified 1,716 DE genes; carbohydrate metabolism, hormone metabolism, ROS scavenging, and epigenetic-modification genes were enriched/upregulated in higher-yield self-rooting juvenile clones. The study interpreted these changes as providing a basis for improved latex metabolism and flow, but it did not directly compare long-term versus short-term flowing trees.

source_tools.relevance: Primary comparative transcriptome study abstract states the clone groups, DEG count, and implicated pathways.

key_findings.finding: Ethylene/ethephon transcriptomics provide mechanistic support for prolonged flow and regeneration, with an important tradeoff toward tapping-panel dryness. PMID 26985821 used an EST microarray in mature virgin trees at 8, 24, and 48 h after ethephon; 163 genes changed (92 up, 71 down). Candidate processes were laticifer water circulation, ROS production/scavenging, sugar metabolism, and actin-cytoskeleton assembly/depolymerization; ethephon increased flow duration and reduced plugging index. PMID 27008913 profiled bark at 8 and 24 h after ethephon and found 10,216 and 9,374 DEGs, respectively; glycolysis and Calvin-cycle/carbon-fixation genes were induced, whereas IPP/rubber-biosynthesis pathway enrichment was not significant. The authors proposed increased precursor/carbon flux, with Calvin-cycle activity potentially contributing to durability of stimulation. These are treatment-response studies, not direct long-term-flow versus short-term-flow comparisons.

source_tools.relevance: Primary microarray study directly reports time course, DE genes, flow-duration phenotype, and candidate processes.
Primary ethephon bark transcriptome study reports time points, DEG counts, glycolysis/Calvin-cycle interpretation, and durability claim.

key_findings.finding: Ethylene-associated transcriptomic evidence also links prolonged flow to water transport and redox control. PMID 25927524 characterized the latex-abundant aquaporin HbPIP2;3: its transcript was induced by wounding and Ethrel, associated with clonal yield potential and Ethrel response, and interpreted as central to laticifer water balance. PMID 27419133 found Hbγ-ECS1 expression increased with tapping and Ethrel, correlated with thiol/glutathione-related antioxidant content, and was related to duration of latex flow in long-term flowing latex. These studies provide plausible physiological mechanisms—water influx/fluidity and delayed coagulation/ROS buffering—but are focused gene studies rather than global comparative transcriptomics.

source_tools.relevance: Primary study links HbPIP2;3 expression, water conductance, tapping/Ethrel response, and yield.
Primary study directly reports Hbγ-ECS1 expression in long-term flowing latex and association with flow duration and thiols.

key_findings.finding: Redox and latex-regeneration studies extend the mechanism but do not establish prolonged-flow causality. PMID 30952924 analyzed laticifer redox genes and degradome/small-RNA regulation: 161 redox-related genes were expressed in latex and 13 were targeted by 11 miRNAs, including a notable miR398/CuZnSOD regulatory feature; the reported material was long-term-flow RRIM600 latex, but there was no long-term versus short-term comparator. PMID 34764965 identified 3,626 snoRNAs, 50 highly expressed in latex, 13 positively correlated with adjusted TSC, and HbsnoR28 strongly correlated with latex regeneration using an insulated tapping system; this addresses regeneration rather than sustained post-tapping flow.

key_findings.finding: Tapping-response transcriptome/proteome studies explain regeneration and harvesting-induced production but not long-term flow per se. PMID 35222526 followed virgin/resting trees through the first five tappings and identified 505 DE transcript-derived fragments plus 117 DE protein spots; sugar transport/metabolism and rubber-biosynthesis transcripts were generally induced, with strong validation of 29 regeneration-related transcripts. PMID 29855601 compared ethephon-treated slight/severe TPD and untreated slight-TPD latex: 8,111 DEGs responded to ethephon in slight TPD and 728 in ethephon-induced severe TPD, highlighting metabolism, wounding, and depressed jasmonate responses in TPD. These findings support regeneration and the boundary between stimulation and flow failure, but do not prove a mechanism of sustained flow in healthy long-term-flow trees.

source_tools.relevance: Primary integrative tapping study reports design, DEG/protein counts, pathways, and regeneration validation.
Primary latex RNA-seq TPD/ethephon study reports treatment groups, DEG counts, and hormone/stress network findings.

key_findings.finding: Overall conclusion: transcriptome and comparative transcriptomic analyses have revealed a coherent candidate mechanism for sustained latex flow—ethylene/wounding-responsive enhancement of laticifer water influx and latex dilution, carbohydrate/central-carbon supply, antioxidant and thiol buffering, reduced rubber-particle aggregation/coagulation, and cell-wall/cytoskeletal properties—while latex regeneration additionally involves jasmonate, sugar/MVA-rubber precursor metabolism, and regulatory noncoding RNAs. However, direct evidence remains limited: only PMID 25928745 explicitly compared clones differing in flow duration, and most studies infer prolonged-flow mechanisms from yield, ethephon response, regeneration, or long-term-flow samples without a matched short-term/non-flowing control or functional perturbation.
